correctness.rationale: An identifying code meets every closed ball and every pairwise symmetric difference of closed balls. Independently, python3 /workspace/reproductions/4.py exhausts all 8008 and 11440 candidates at sizes six and seven using these transversal constraints; it finds zero and 960 respectively. The constraints are monotone, excluding smaller sizes by extension. Any automorphism fixing zero permutes its four neighbors, and vertex weights and distances to these four neighbors determine each bit, proving that translations and bit permutations exhaust the automorphism group. Orbit traversal by the four bit translations and three adjacent swaps gives disjoint orbits of the displayed representatives of sizes 192,384,384 exhausting the 960, with the stated Hamming pair-distance profiles. Orbit–stabilizer gives the asserted orders; the double coordinate swap directly fixes the symmetric representative. The four-entry Gray map identifies each Lee 4-cycle with a binary 2-cube, and the two quaternary examples as transcribed in the frozen package give profiles (4,9,6,2) and (6,7,6,2). That calculation verifies the comparison conditional on the transcription, not the exact primary text. The finite enumeration establishes the classification independently of the Kim–Kim census.

value.rationale: A complete classification of this natural equality layer is useful in principle. As a separate finding on the evidence available, however, the explicitly available equivalent orbit table exhausts that value: orders and distance profiles are mechanical consequences of its representative sets and sizes. Displaying the nontrivial double swap and comparing two historical transcriptions does not provide a separate useful unknown invariant. This is not rejection on the ground that the theorem is finite.
